projects.name: Veil Nebula - Full Complex
projects.target: Cygnus Loop — NGC 6960 (Western Veil) + Pickering's Triangle + NGC 6992/6995 (Eastern Veil)
projects.frameMode: Reducer, 280mm f/3.9 — single frame, whole complex (no mosaic)
projects.notes: Whole Cygnus Loop (~3°) fits one reducer frame at 27° — no mosaic. OIII is strong across the loop (including the fainter Western Veil). SII is the weakest channel; prioritize it at a dark site. Re-shoot flats if rotation changes.

projects.name: North America Nebula - First Light
projects.target: NGC 7000 / Caldwell 20 (North America Nebula); Pelican Nebula (IC 5070) adjacent across L935
projects.frameMode: Reducer 280mm f/3.9 · Bin2 — single frame (continent ~2°×1.7° fits easily)
projects.anchorStar: Deneb (α Cyg) — finder reference ~3° west; HD 199579 (mag ~6) near the Gulf of Mexico
projects.notes: Ha-dominant emission nebula in Cygnus (~2,590 ly). Classic SHO target: Ha carries the continent shape; OIII/SII add structure along the Gulf and coasts. Reducer FOV (3.91°×2.66°) easily holds NGC 7000 alone; a slight west shift can pull in Pelican (IC 5070) if desired. Shot 2026-07-20 from NYC home (Bortle 9), reducer Bin2 — 30 min Ha, 15 min OIII, 15 min SII.

assets.name: ZWO AM3N Harmonic Drive
assets.notes: B&H AM3N+TC40 kit ($1,800) — mount share allocated $1,420
specs: Bluetooth direct, or WiFi via hand controller / ASIAIR
quirks: No clutches. Axes move electronically only — forcing them by hand can damage the strain-wave gears.
No optical polar scope; polar alignment is done in software via plate-solving (e.g. ASIAIR PA).
Factory PE typically within ±15″ (individual PE report included). Autoguiding is normal for multi-minute subs; guided RMS around 0.5–1.0″ is typical for light refractor loads.
Strain-wave mounts often track more stably slightly east-heavy than perfectly balanced. Rated 8 kg without a counterweight / 13 kg with one.
EQ and alt-az modes; control via Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, hand controller, or USB.

assets.name: ZWO TC40 Carbon Fiber Tripod
assets.notes: From AM3N+TC40 kit — allocated $380 of $1,800. Standalone ZWO list $399 (incl. oversized-ship surcharge).
quirks: Carbon dual-section travel tripod for the AM-series; ~2.3 kg with a high published load rating.
Packs larger than the mount head alone despite the low weight.

assets.name: Askar FRA400 72mm f/5.6
assets.notes: Includes 0.7× reducer + EAF, tube rings, dovetail, handle
specs: Reducer + EAF, tube rings, dovetail, handle
quirks: Two optical regimes: native Petzval is forgiving once focused; with the 0.7× reducer, back focus is strict (55 mm ± ~2 mm from the M48 thread to the sensor). Current reduced stack ≈ 54.6 mm.
Reducer mounts inside the drawtube (M68); camera side is M48. With the reducer, the camera’s contribution in the spacer chain is the 7.5 mm flange distance (adapter moved into the stack).
Focuser rotates 360°; flat frames are specific to camera rotation.

assets.name: ZWO ASI294MM Pro
assets.notes: From $2,100 camera+EFW+filters package — allocated $728 (share of new-retail mix). Dealer new ~$1480.
specs: USB 3.0 to ASIAIR, built-in hub for EFW/EAF
quirks: IMX492 shows amp glow; it calibrates out with darks that match gain, offset, temperature, and exposure.
Very short flats can be nonlinear — exposures of roughly 2–3+ seconds with a dimmer flat source behave more consistently.
Bias frames are generally avoided on this sensor; dark-flats are the usual substitute.
Narrowband flats can show sensor patterning that calibrates out with proper flats.
Microlensing / interference artifacts can appear around very bright stars — a known sensor trait.
TEC cooling: sudden cold power-off risks thermal stress; a warm-up before shutdown is standard practice.

assets.name: ZWO EFW 8×31mm
quirks: Cosmetic scratch on the camera-facing side (disclosed) — no optical effect.
31 mm filters on the 4/3″ ASI294 leave limited clearance (~4.5 mm/side). Faster systems (e.g. f/3.9) show more corner falloff; mild vignetting is typically flat-calibratable.

assets.name: Astrodon / Baader 31mm Filter Set
assets.notes: From $2,100 package — allocated $1225. New equiv ~$2490: Astrodon LRGB $769 + Ha/OIII/SII 5nm $488×3 + Baader Hβ $257.
specs: L, R, G, B, SII, Ha, OIII, Hβ
quirks: Filters in mixed sets are generally not parafocal; EAF per-filter focus offsets are the usual approach.

assets.name: SVBONY SV165 Guide Scope
assets.notes: 30mm f/4 mini guide scope — rings + dovetail included
quirks: Very wide FOV at 120mm — easy guide-star acquisition with small sensors like the ASI120MM Mini.
Helical focuser with a lock; slightly soft guide stars often centroid more stably than razor-sharp ones.
Camera-oriented back focus — some setups need a short extension tube.

assets.name: ZWO ASI120MM Mini
specs: M42×0.75 T-thread, USB 2.0 Type-C, ST4 port
quirks: Open-box unit.
Small 1/3″ sensor (3.75 µm pixels); guide calibration is most stable near the celestial equator and meridian.

assets.name: ZWO ASIAIR Plus 256GB
specs: 2× USB 3.0, 2× USB 2.0, Gigabit Ethernet, USB-C, DSLR shutter
Plate solving, PA, guiding, autofocus, scheduling
quirks: ~6A input ceiling (typically specified 12V/5A, max ~6A shared across its 12V outputs). Cooled cameras and mounts are normally powered from a separate distribution box; ASIAIR is used here as the data/control hub.
ZWO ecosystem control only — it does not drive a Pegasus Powerbox (Powerbox runs standalone after Unity setup).
Control app is mobile-only (iOS/Android); no official desktop client.
Factory Wi-Fi credentials are on the device sticker; Station Mode on home Wi-Fi is supported.

assets.name: Pegasus Powerbox Micro
specs: 2× RCA PWM, auto-dew via env. sensor
One-time via Pegasus Unity, then standalone
quirks: Not controllable from ASIAIR. Configured once in Pegasus Unity, then runs standalone with settings that persist across power cycles.
Built for ~10A-class input; a 5A wall supply is undersized for a full imaging load.
Dew outputs are RCA PWM channels, 5A max each.
Reverse-polarity protected; overvoltage cutoff above ~14.5V input.

assets.name: Anker SOLIX C300 DC
assets.notes: Field battery — wall charger not included. DC-only model (no AC outlets).
specs: 1× car socket 120W, 2× USB-C 140W bidirectional, 1× USB-C 100W, 1× USB-C 15W, 2× USB-A 12W
Dual USB-C PD to ~80% in ~1h; solar or car
quirks: DC-only model — no AC outlets (unlike the AC C300). Field 12V comes from the car socket; USB ports for devices/charging.
First activation needs USB-C PD ≥18W on USB-C2 or USB-C3 only.
Wall charger is not included in the box.
Solar input: XT60, 11–28V. Not compatible with Anker PS30 / other 5V USB-C panels, PS200, or PS400.

assets.notes: Includes BTF-LIGHTING 12V 10A supply. Mixed commodity accessories — no single product release date.
